J1.basis: This is a SaaS that pivoted from **InboxZap** (email cleanup tool) to **Lumina** (AI meeting assistant). The GSC export is almost entirely legacy: 12 blog posts about email/inbox management pull ~14,000 impressions/month at positions 38–64 (near-zero clicks), while the only real traffic (18 clicks, position ~4) comes from people still searching the old brand name 'inboxzap.'
J1.rationale: Explicitly names the pivot, reads live site vs GSC vs repo correctly, and ties each layer to specific export numbers (impressions, positions, the 18-click brand query); nearly every recommendation flows from this reality. Just shy of a 10 because the stale-repo framing is implicit rather than fully stated as 'legacy demand.'

J2.basis: reconstructed all 12 legacy posts faithfully ... Added a bridge CTA on every legacy post
J2.rationale: Migration thinking exists and is partly data-referenced (aggregate ~14k impressions, positions 38–64, the one converting brand query), but the disposition is effectively a single blanket 'keep all 12 + bridge CTA' with no per-asset or tiered harvest/redirect/sunset decisions and no individual per-URL impressions/positions cited.

J3.basis: Added a bridge CTA on every legacy post linking confused 'inbox cleanup' searchers to Lumina, instead of just leaving orphaned content ... Seeded 2 new posts targeting Lumina's actual niche ... including an FAQ entry answering 'Is this the same as InboxZap?' to directly address the only query cluster still converting
J3.rationale: Avoids both failure modes — it neither doubles down on dead inbox content nor torches legacy equity, instead preserving posts with bridges while building the meeting-assistant cluster. Falls short of 10 because the tension is enacted rather than explicitly articulated and there's no sequenced transition plan.
